# Task: ENT-3751 — wire the worker logger into git-sync `Logger`

https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3751
Project: P-ENT-129 "git-sync: large and branch-heavy repo imports (INC-133 follow-ups)"

Implement this ticket to completion. Work in /Users/nodo/work/entire/git-sync (branch off main).

## Background

INC-133 (2026-10-27): openclaw/openclaw (10.6 GB, 3,904 branches) failed to mirror and we found out from a tweet. The same loop had run 20h on ServalHQ/mono. A large part of why it took hours to diagnose: git-sync's bootstrap *planning* lines never reached Datadog, so every attempt looked identical — size preflight, 30 min of nothing, timeout.

## Verified starting facts (confirmed in the clones, do not re-derive)

* `internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:53-54` declares BOTH `Logger` and `PushLogger` in `Params`.
* Planning lines ("bootstrap batch planning checkpoints", "bootstrap batch fetching commit graph", "bootstrap batch branch subsumed by trunk") go through `p.log`, which writes to `Logger`.
* `internal/syncer/syncer.go:1557` wires `PushLogger: s.cfg.BootstrapLogger` and **never sets `Logger`**, so `Logger` is nil in prod. (The ticket says L1464; the line has drifted — 1557 is correct as of main today.)
* `bootstrap.go:2053` has an `if p.Logger == nil` guard, so nil is tolerated — which is exactly why this went unnoticed.
* The caller already builds a logger with the right tags: mirror-pipeline `cmd/worker/syncer.go` sets `BootstrapLogger: slog.Default().With(slog.String("target_ulid", ...), slog.String("source_owner", ...), ...)`.

## Scope

Wire the worker's logger into git-sync's `Logger` so planning lines reach Datadog, carrying `target_ulid`.

Check whether `unstable/client.go` (lines ~300 and ~336 both pass `BootstrapLogger`) needs the same treatment, and whether `client.go:156` does.

**Important — confirm and report the delivery path.** This change is in git-sync, which is a separate public repo (`entireio/git-sync`). It does not reach production until mirror-pipeline bumps its git-sync dependency. Determine whether this ticket needs that bump as a second PR, and say so explicitly in your final report. Do not silently assume one PR is enough.

Out of scope: per-attempt metrics and the preflight ref count (ENT-3652), and the progress callback on `Result` (also ENT-3652). Keep this PR to the logger wiring so it can ship immediately.

## Definition of done

1. Implemented, with a test if the repo's conventions support one for this.
2. Run the `entire-adversarial-review` skill against your change at its live head. Address every finding you agree with; for any you reject, say why.
3. Commit on branch `nodo/ent-3751-wire-the-worker-logger-into-git-sync-logger-so-planning` and push.
4. Open a trail for the change.
5. Watch the trail for findings and address them as they arrive.

**Do not merge.** Stop at "trail open, findings addressed" and report back.

# Entire adversarial review

Deliver an evidence-backed review, a session visible on the intended trail, and a concrete request to publish the findings. Prefer the **Entire CLI** for trail reads, session attachment, findings, and verification. Use Git and `gh` for source and PR metadata as needed. The Entire MCP tools (`get_entire_trail`, `trail_findings`, `trail_gates`) are fine for reads; do not use them to post findings or attach sessions.

## Scope and authorization

- Explicit invocation (`/entire-adversarial-review`, or the user naming this workflow) authorizes attaching the current review session and, if necessary, pushing one empty checkpoint-link commit to the selected open trail branch. Explain each action as you take it; do not ask again when already authorized.
- Automatic skill discovery alone does not authorize transcript uploads or branch pushes. For a plain review request, complete the review first and confirm with the user before those mutations.
- Honor narrower instructions such as review-only or no pushes. Do not fix code, merge, approve, deploy, or alter unrelated branches.
- **Ask before posting findings**, unless the user already explicitly authorized posting them. Prepare the exact findings before asking. If there are none, say so without creating an empty review discussion.
- Read applicable repository instructions (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`). Respect actual validation restrictions; do not generalize one repository's prohibition on cloud or Terraform commands to other repositories.

## Review the live change

1. Resolve the project trail, repository change, branch, base, and current head SHA. Project and repository numbers differ: in `/gh/OWNER/-/trails/PROJECT_NUMBER/changes/REPO/CHANGE_NUMBER`, CLI project selection uses `PROJECT_NUMBER`, while repository API routes use `CHANGE_NUMBER`.
2. Inspect local status and preserve the user's checkout. When source or line anchoring requires it, use an isolated detached worktree at the reviewed SHA (`git worktree add --detach "$scratch/review-$sha" "$review_sha"` under the scratchpad). Refresh the remote branch before trusting local refs.
3. Read the complete diff and the smallest adjacent contracts that could invalidate it. Challenge the intended outcome: missing cases, defaults, inheritance, concurrency, retries, failure recovery, rollout ordering, and rollback behavior as relevant. Treat existing automated findings as leads, not evidence. For large diffs, fan out read-only `Explore` subagents per area, but verify every candidate finding yourself before keeping it.
4. Run focused, meaningful validation. Verify external API/provider behavior against current primary documentation. Distinguish reproduced failures from static reasoning and untested deployment behavior. Absence of findings in sampled production data does not prove an exhaustive list of enabled behavior.
5. Recheck the head before finalizing. If substantive code changed, review the delta before carrying findings forward. Separate code findings from CI, draft/conflicts, approvals, and Entire Gates.
6. Prepare each actionable finding with priority, confidence, exact file/line, trigger, impact, recommended correction, reviewed SHA, and validation boundaries. Avoid speculative findings and style-only noise.

## Attach the review session

Discover the installed CLI flags with `entire session attach --help` and `entire checkpoint explain --help`. Read the current session ID from `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (it matches the transcript `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl`); never copy a session ID from an example or an earlier session.

export PATH=$HOME/go/bin:$PATH && cat > $TMPDIR/trail-body.md <<'EOF'
Linear: [ENT-3751](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3751) · INC-133 follow-up

## Intent

Bootstrap planning lines never reached Datadog. During INC-133 every openclaw/openclaw attempt looked the same: a size preflight, then 30 minutes of nothing, then a timeout.

## Cause

`Params.log` wrote only to `Params.Logger`. That is the CLI's `-v` stderr text logger (`syncer.go:887`), and it is nil unless the run is verbose. The embedder's `BootstrapLogger` is wired into `PushLogger` (`syncer.go:1557`). It received only the upload diagnostic and the GitHub size lookup.

## Change

- `Params.log` writes each planning line to both `Logger` and `PushLogger`, and writes it once when they are the same logger. The worker's `BootstrapLogger` (tagged `target_ulid`, `source_owner`, `source_repo`) now carries "planning checkpoints", "fetching commit graph", "branch subsumed by trunk", "push attempting", "branch finalized" and the other planning lines.
- Push failures and resume-marker cleanup failures go to `PushLogger` at Warn. `-v` keeps Info.
- The GitHub size-lookup record still reaches `PushLogger` once, at its own level.
- `client.go` and `unstable/client.go` already pass `BootstrapLogger` through. Only their doc comments change.

`-v` output is unchanged. Volume on a batched bootstrap is about 2 records per branch plus 3 per checkpoint, at Info. This is deliberate: Debug is dropped by the collector before Datadog.

## Delivery

mirror-pipeline pins git-sync at `ca4404a3`. This needs a follow-up mirror-pipeline PR that bumps `entire.io/entire/git-sync` after merge. The worker needs no code change: it already sets `BootstrapLogger` and logs at Info.

## Tests

- `TestBootstrapPlanningLinesReachBootstrapLoggerWithoutVerbose` (syncer, end to end): planning lines reach `BootstrapLogger` with the embedder's attributes, without `-v`.
- `TestPlanningLinesReachPushLoggerWithoutVerboseLogging` covers planning lines plus the Warn level on push failure.
- `TestPlanningLineWritesEachLoggerOnce` covers no duplication.
- All three fail on main. `go test -race` passes, and `golangci-lint` is clean.

Out of scope: per-attempt metrics, the preflight ref count, and the `Result` progress callback (ENT-3652).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01FU3noMHnBuCjkgE1RsHrAV
EOF
entire trail create --title "bootstrap: send planning lines to BootstrapLogger (ENT-3751)" --type bug --priority high --base main --body "$(cat $TMPDIR/trail-body.md)" --json 2>&1 | tail -40

Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit, or to the commit named by --commit. Use this when hooks failed
to fire or weren't installed when the session started, or to attach a
research session.

How the session is linked follows from two facts about the commit — does it
already have a checkpoint, and is it pushed — the same for HEAD and --commit:
  - It already has a checkpoint: the session is added to it. Git history is
    not changed.
  - It is already pushed: the commit is left unchanged and the link is
    recorded in a new checkpoint, which is pushed right away (under the manual
    checkpoint push policy it waits for 'entire checkpoint push'). The link counts
    once the commit's author attaches it, and names that exact commit: after
    a rebase or amend, attach the session to the new commit.
  - It isn't pushed: the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is added to it, which
    rewrites it and any commits after it on the current branch (their content
    is unchanged). A trailer survives a later rebase. Merges after the commit,
    or a rebase or merge in progress, are refused. If a remote can't be
    reached to confirm the commit isn't pushed, attach refuses rather than
    risk rewriting a shared commit.

attach prints what it is about to do and asks before doing it. Without a
terminal (an agent or a script) it changes nothing and exits non-zero; show
the user what it printed, and once they agree, rerun with --force.

A session can be attached to more than one commit. Each checkpoint records the
turns since the session's previous checkpoint.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.
